title: Design System & Component Library
prompt: Design a shared frontend component library for several product teams. Cover tokens, accessible primitives, controlled APIs, theming, packaging and safe upgrades. Use a small documentation/catalog app as the browser architecture; do not turn this into a backend service design. Draw the component/data-flow architecture, define state owners and contracts, and explain performance, accessibility and recovery. No UI coding is required.
functionalReqs: Compose primitives into product patterns without duplicating behavior
Support themes, localization and controlled/uncontrolled APIs
Ship versioned packages with documentation and migration guidance
nonFunctionalReqs: 20 consuming apps, ~40 primitives; avoid bundling the full library for one button; measure consumer output, not source size.
Define keyboard/focus contracts per primitive, native semantics first, contrast and reduced-motion tokens, accessible-name requirements and automated plus manual assistive-technology checks.
Document stable token/API contracts, use prerelease consumer validation, migration tooling and version rollback. Accessibility requirements are part of the API.

scale.notes: 20 consuming apps, ~40 primitives; avoid bundling the full library for one button; measure consumer output, not source size.
scale.storage: Consumer imports 1 Button from a 40-component library; illustrative interview assumptions, not measured guarantees.

outOfScope: Backend sharding, ranking algorithms and infrastructure provisioning
Implementing a production UI inside this exercise
deepDives: Layer semantic tokens -> headless behavior primitives -> styled components -> product patterns. Define one controlled/uncontrolled ownership rule and forward refs. Publish tree-shakable per-component exports, semver changes and migration examples with visual, interaction and accessibility coverage.
A theme override or minor release breaks a consumer interaction
Headless primitives maximize flexibility but consumers must style correctly. A styled system accelerates consistency but needs deliberate escape hatches; avoid unrestricted internal DOM dependencies.
